title: Running Frontier-Class AI Models Across 8 NVIDIA DGX Spark Nodes | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: At GTC Berlin NVIDIA announced official eight-node DGX Spark clusters with 1 TB of unified memory, enough to serve the full 753B-parameter GLM 5.3 from Z.ai locally. Benchmarks show decode on Qwen3.8-27B scaling from about 12 to 52 tokens per second with the new RoCEnante collective backend (4.43x at eight nodes), NeMo Switchyard routing raising cluster throughput up to 3x, and nanochat pre-training scaling 7.79x at 97.4% efficiency.

themes.theme: Eight-node clusters and 1 TB local memory

insights.claim: NVIDIA announced at GTC Berlin official support for eight-node DGX Spark clusters, scaling unified memory from 128 GB per node to 1 TB, with eight-node support in NVIDIA Sync's Cluster Assistant coming by the end of the year.
insights.speaker: Arvind Gopalakrishnan
insights.so_what: Multi-node desk clusters raise the per-customer unit volume of DGX Spark sales and push local AI into frontier-model territory.
insights.locator: At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA announced official

insights.claim: An eight-node DGX Spark cluster can serve the full 753B-parameter GLM 5.3 model from Z.ai, about 470 GB in NVFP4, which would not start on a four-node system, and GLM 5.3 Flash ran at roughly 80 tokens per second in generation on eight nodes.
insights.speaker: Arvind Gopalakrishnan
insights.so_what: Frontier-scale Chinese open-weight models running on local NVIDIA hardware broaden on-prem demand and reduce reliance on cloud APIs.
insights.quote: making it one of the largest open models you can serve locally.

insights.claim: NVIDIA's Spark-optimized RoCEnante collective backend replaces multi-round ring all-reduce with a single-kernel all-to-all exchange plus local reduction, cutting latency for the small-message, low-concurrency tensor-parallel decode typical of local AI hardware at the cost of more data movement.
insights.speaker: Arvind Gopalakrishnan
insights.so_what: Software-level collective optimizations extract more performance from existing Spark hardware, improving the value of multi-node purchases.
insights.quote: The main benefit is fewer communication steps.
insights.locator: Faster collectives with a Spark-optimized backend

insights.claim: On Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 over a switch topology, RoCEnante delivered a 4.43x decode speedup at eight DGX Spark nodes versus 3.05x without it, plus about 5% higher prefill and 21% higher decode at four nodes and about 18% higher decode at eight nodes on the non-quantized model.
insights.speaker: Arvind Gopalakrishnan
insights.so_what: A 45% scaling-efficiency gain makes eight-node clusters materially more attractive than four-node ones.
insights.quote: At eight Spark nodes, ROCEnante delivers a 4.43x speedup vs. 3.05x without it—a 45% improvement in scaling efficiency.

insights.claim: RoCEnante is merged into FlashInfer, falls back to NCCL if its startup test fails, works only on switch-connected topologies, and is not a replacement for NCCL, which remains the default and the better choice at high concurrency or larger cluster sizes; the original one-shot all-reduce approach came from community contributor Jason Cook (el8).
insights.speaker: Arvind Gopalakrishnan
insights.so_what: Upstreaming into FlashInfer spreads the optimization across the open inference ecosystem built on NVIDIA hardware.
insights.locator: The backend applies only to switch-connected

insights.claim: In NVIDIA's benchmark of dense Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 without speculative decoding, DGX Spark decode throughput scaled from 11.86 tokens per second on one node to 52.58 on eight switch-connected nodes (4.43x), while prefill scaled only to 1.94x (2,635 to 5,105 TPS).
insights.speaker: Arvind Gopalakrishnan
insights.so_what: Decode scales well but prefill scales sublinearly, so long-context workloads gain less from extra Spark nodes.
insights.locator: Two, four, eight: Scaling the cluster

insights.claim: NVIDIA says a switchless physical ring is the simplest, lowest-cost choice for four-node DGX Spark inference because NCCL defaults to ring algorithms, but a switch is required to scale to eight nodes with split allocations, to run all-to-all or MPI-style HPC workloads, or to use the RoCEnante backend.
insights.speaker: Arvind Gopalakrishnan
insights.so_what: Eight-node deployments pull through networking-switch sales alongside Spark units.
insights.locator: Switchless ring topology and setup simplicity

insights.claim: NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard uses a lightweight classifier to route each request to a model pool; in NVIDIA's prototype, OpenBMB's MiniCPM5 2B handled classification and simple tasks while Qwen3.8 Flash Next handled complex ones, and the routed agent scored 91/100 on a 92-case tool-use benchmark, matching the Qwen-only setup.
insights.speaker: Arvind Gopalakrishnan
insights.so_what: Model routing that keeps quality while cutting cost is becoming a standard part of agent infrastructure, which pressures large-model inference pricing.

insights.claim: Because MiniCPM serves about an order of magnitude more requests per second per replica than Qwen, an eight-node DGX Spark cluster with three Qwen and two MiniCPM replicas reached about 1.5x aggregate throughput over a Qwen-only baseline when half of requests went to Qwen, and about 3.0x when a quarter did.
insights.speaker: Arvind Gopalakrishnan
insights.so_what: Routing traffic to small models multiplies effective capacity on fixed hardware, which favors small-model providers.

insights.claim: Pre-training an approximately 896.5M-parameter nanochat model from scratch across eight DGX Spark nodes achieved a 7.79x speedup at 97.4% scaling efficiency (8,741 to 68,079 tokens per second), because with full model copies per node the only cross-node traffic is per-step gradient synchronization.
insights.speaker: Arvind Gopalakrishnan
insights.so_what: Makes desk-side Spark clusters a credible small-model training platform, which extends their market beyond inference.
insights.quote: Eight nodes deliver a 7.79x speedup at 97.4% efficiency
insights.locator: Pre-training from scratch: near-linear scaling with nanochat

insights.claim: NVIDIA pitches eight-node DGX Spark clusters as an on-ramp to prototype and pre-train models locally and then scale out as models grow.
insights.speaker: Arvind Gopalakrishnan
insights.so_what: This land-and-expand strategy channels local developers toward NVIDIA data-center GPUs.
insights.quote: Prototype and pre-train locally, then scale out as the model grows.
